mnemonic: Two different characters for the same idea stacked on top of each other, held back and shut in, and somebody in the office knows anyway: ひみつ.
sentence: これは秘密です。
sentence_meaning: This is a secret.

mnemonic: A roof 屋 with that much ground spread out 敷 underneath it, and nobody has lived in it for forty years. The rumour is it is haunted: やしき.
notes: Near 意識 いしき, consciousness, in sound and nothing else.
sentence: その屋敷には幽霊が出るという噂だ。
sentence_meaning: It's a rumor (saying) that house is haunted.

mnemonic: The point where the world 界 stops going your way 限 and you stop with it. Her patience got there about an hour ago: げんかい.
sentence: もう我慢の限界です。
sentence_meaning: This is the limit of my self-control.

mnemonic: Winning 勝 and losing 負 bolted into the one word, which is what a contest actually is. It has only just started: しょうぶ.
sentence: 勝負はまだ始まったばかりよ。
sentence_meaning: The match has just started.

mnemonic: A small sun 日 that came to life 生 an enormous distance off. Clear night, and you can pick out dozens of them: ほし.
sentence: 今夜は星がよく見えます。
sentence_meaning: You can see the stars well tonight.

mnemonic: Sun 日 and moon 月 both up at once and both of them looking straight at it. Nobody in the room needs it explained: あきらか.
notes: 当たり前 あたりまえ is obvious as in what anybody would expect. 明らか is obvious because it is there in front of you.
sentence: 明らかに彼が悪い。
sentence_meaning: It's clearly his fault.

mnemonic: The heart 忄 goes round the same thing at two in the morning and arrives back where it set off. The entrance exams, again: なやむ.
notes: 困る こまる is being stuck by a problem sitting in front of you, and 心配 しんぱい is the worry itself. 悩む is turning a thing over inside your own head.
sentence: 彼は受験のことで悩んでいます。
sentence_meaning: He's worried about entrance examinations.

mnemonic: Everything gathered 集 into the middle 中 of one thing with nothing left over for anything else. Books open, phone in a drawer: しゅうちゅう.
sentence: 勉強に集中しなさい。
sentence_meaning: Concentrate on studying.

meaning: to be mistaken, to be incorrect
mnemonic: There is a gap 間 between what you think and what is so, and your feet took the other way round it 違. You are wrong: まちがう.
sentence: あなたは間違っている。
sentence_meaning: You're mistaken.

mnemonic: Turn the cloth over and there is the face of it nobody was meant to look at. Round the back of the office there is a park: うら.
notes: 逆 ぎゃく is reverse as in the opposite direction and 背中 せなか is the back on your body. 裏 is the other side of a thing.
sentence: 会社の裏に公園があります。
sentence_meaning: There's a park behind the company.

mnemonic: Spread far enough that the light comes through, and the soup has had the same treatment. You can taste the water in it: うすい.
notes: 弱い よわい is weak as in not strong. 薄い is weak as in thin, watery or pale. Near 上手い うまい in sound only.
sentence: この料理は味が薄い。
sentence_meaning: This food is flavored lightly.

meaning: to wish, to ask a favor, to pray
mnemonic: A head 頁 bowed over the same plain 原 request night after night, asking for one man to get well again: ねがう.
sentence: 彼が元気になるよう願っています。
sentence_meaning: We're praying that he gets well.

mnemonic: Round 回 the long way and back 復 to where the body started out. It took a month and now it is as though nothing happened: かいふく.
sentence: 体がすっかり回復した。
sentence_meaning: My body completely recovered.

meaning: to let flow, to set adrift
mnemonic: You stop holding it and let the water 氵 have it. She did not wipe her face, she simply let them go: ながす.
notes: Near 長い ながい, long, in sound and nothing else.
sentence: 彼女は涙を流したんだ。
sentence_meaning: She shed tears.

mnemonic: The teacher talked for forty minutes and the boy did not shift once, not a foot, not a hand. Fixed to the spot: じっと.
notes: One of a family with もっと, ずっと, きっと, やっと and そっと, which share the ending and nothing else at all.
sentence: あの生徒はじっと先生の話を聞いていたね。
sentence_meaning: That pupil listened quietly to the teacher.

mnemonic: The thing 物 down at the root 本 of it and not the copy in the window. That stone on her hand is the actual one: ほんもの.
sentence: これは本物のダイヤモンドです。
sentence_meaning: This is a real diamond.

mnemonic: The foot comes down exactly 正 on the line and there is nothing to argue about. He is a hero, and that is the word for it: まさに.
notes: Near まさか, which does the opposite job, no way. 正に confirms and まさか disbelieves.
sentence: 彼は正に英雄ね。
sentence_meaning: He's truly a hero.

mnemonic: You take 取 hold of the thing and put it back 戻 where it belongs, and what he got back this time was his own confidence: とりもどす.
notes: 回復 かいふく is the recovery happening to you. 取り戻す is you going and getting the thing back.
sentence: 彼はやっと自信を取り戻した。
sentence_meaning: He finally got back his confidence.

mnemonic: Better than 何 anything else anybody could name, and the thing that actually mattered was that you got here in one piece: なにより.
sentence: ご無事で何よりです。
sentence_meaning: The most important thing is that you're safe.

mnemonic: Two characters for the body put together into one word, which is what makes it the formal one. A sound mind lives in one of these: しんたい.
notes: からだ is the everyday reading of 体, and 身 み on its own is your own person rather than the flesh. しんたい is the stiff word, for health checks and proverbs.
sentence: 健康な身体には健全な精神が宿る。
sentence_meaning: A sound mind in a sound body.

mnemonic: A thing that points a way 方 and a window that opens one way only 向, and every one of them is looking down it: ほうこう.
notes: 方法 ほうほう is a method, how you do a thing. 方向 is which way you are pointing.
sentence: あの人たちは皆、同じ方向を見ている。
sentence_meaning: Those people are all looking in the same direction.

meaning: to pass, to take, to go through
mnemonic: The road 辶 carries on all the way through instead of stopping short, and you are down it every single morning: とおる.
notes: 通り とおり is the street itself. 通る glosses as to take because you take a road, not the way かかる takes time.
sentence: 毎日、この道を通ります。
sentence_meaning: I take this road every day.

mnemonic: Empty 空 gap 間 with nothing in it at all, until somebody puts a great deal of furniture into a very small one: くうかん.
notes: 部屋 へや is a room with walls. 空間 is the space itself, and 余裕 よゆう is room as spare capacity.
sentence: 狭い空間に物がたくさん置いてあるね。
sentence_meaning: A lot of things have been put into a tight space.

mnemonic: Whatever was travelling has come down 着 and stopped moving, and at ten o'clock that is you, at the office: つく.
notes: Same reading as 付く つく, to attach, and つく, to be switched on. The character is the one in 着る, to wear, and both are about something coming to rest on a thing.
sentence: 10時に会社に着きます。
sentence_meaning: I arrive at the office at 10 A.M.

mnemonic: What you are allowed 可 to do meets what you are able 能 to do, and twenty kilos in a year sits somewhere along that line: かのう.
sentence: 20キロのダイエットは可能だと思いますか。
sentence_meaning: Do you think a diet to lose 20kg is possible?

mnemonic: An axe 斤 taken to a standing 立 tree 木, and what comes of it is not repair work but a fresh start. The plan is under way: あらた.
notes: 新しい あたらしい is the everyday new. 新た is stiffer and goes in front of a noun: 新たな計画.
sentence: 新たな計画が進んでいます。
sentence_meaning: A new plan is in progress.

mnemonic: Not a bit more than expected, a great deal more, and he came out of there hours before anybody had him down for: ずいぶん.
sentence: 随分早く終わったね。
sentence_meaning: You finished really early, didn't you?

mnemonic: Both hands out and a mouth going, groping after a thing you cannot see. She stopped a stranger and asked the way: たずねる.
notes: 聞く きく is asking a question. 尋ねる is going looking for the answer, and it is the formal one.
sentence: 彼女は道を尋ねた。
sentence_meaning: She asked for directions.

mnemonic: It started life as a tree 木 and finished with four legs and a back, holding exactly one person. You pull it out and sit down: いす.
sentence: 椅子に座ります。
sentence_meaning: I will sit on the chair.

mnemonic: Earth 土 piled up and worked at until it holds 成, and four hundred and fifty years later it is still standing there: しろ.
sentence: この城は４５０年前に建てられました。
sentence_meaning: This castle was built 450 years ago.

mnemonic: There is fear 恐 sitting in the character, and this is the probably you reach for when you would rather it went the other way: おそらく.
notes: 多分 たぶん is the neutral probably. 恐らく is formal, and leans toward the outcome you were hoping to avoid.
sentence: 明日は恐らく晴れるでしょう。
sentence_meaning: The weather will probably clear up tomorrow.

mnemonic: A leaf picked off the bush, dried, and poured out hot, with the お on the front because nobody says it bare. Shall I make some: おちゃ.
sentence: お茶を入れましょうか。
sentence_meaning: Shall I make tea?

mnemonic: Cloud along the top and everything coming down underneath it, drawn as it falls. It has been at this since the morning: あめ.
sentence: 雨が降っています。
sentence_meaning: It's raining.

mnemonic: He got his coat on and went, saying いや the whole way down the path, and he still went. Doing it, and hating every step: いやいや.
sentence: その子はいやいや学校へ行ったの。
sentence_meaning: That child reluctantly went to school.

meaning: the very thing, the picture of
mnemonic: Not merely healthy. The thing itself, as though somebody had drawn health and then put a face on it: そのもの.
sentence: 彼は健康そのものです。
sentence_meaning: He is a picture of health.

mnemonic: The room 室 where the teaching 教 happens, thirty of them in it and the teacher at the front: きょうしつ.
sentence: 先生は教室にいます。
sentence_meaning: The teacher is in the classroom.

mnemonic: A horse 馬 and a deer 鹿 in the one word, out of an old story about a man insisting the one was the other. I was that man: ばか.
sentence: 私は馬鹿だった。
sentence_meaning: I was foolish.

mnemonic: You keep your distance 遠, weigh 慮 whether to say it, and then say nothing. Do not do that, tell me whatever you like: えんりょ.
sentence: 遠慮しないで、何でも言ってください。
sentence_meaning: Please don't hesitate to tell me anything.

mnemonic: The reply was due today, it is ten to six, and you have not started. Not a disaster yet, but it is heading that way: まずい.
notes: The same word まずい also means bad-tasting. This one is a situation going wrong.
sentence: 今日中に返答しなければまずい。
sentence_meaning: If I don't reply by the end of today, I'll be in trouble.

mnemonic: You get through half of it out of politeness and put the fork down. There is no kind way to say it: まずい.
notes: The same word まずい also covers a situation being problematic. This one is about food, where 悪い わるい would be bad in general.
sentence: ここの料理はまずい。
sentence_meaning: The food here is bad.

mnemonic: Everything else he wanted is gone and he is down to asking for one thing. If nothing else, promise me this much: せめて.
notes: 少なくとも すくなくとも puts a floor under a number. せめて is at least as in if nothing else, and it is pleading. At least is not at last: やっと and ようやく are at last.
sentence: せめてこれだけは約束してください。
sentence_meaning: Please promise only this at least.

meaning: to welcome, to go out to meet, to invite
mnemonic: You do not sit at home waiting, you go out down the road 辶 to where they are landing. She will be at the airport when it comes in: むかえる.
sentence: 姉が空港まで迎えに来てくれます。
sentence_meaning: My big sister is coming to pick me up at the airport.

mnemonic: Take the smallest 少 figure you could possibly get away with and it is still two weeks. That is the floor, not the estimate: すくなくとも.
notes: せめて is at least as in if nothing else. 少なくとも puts a floor under a number. At least is not at last: やっと and ようやく are at last.
sentence: この仕事には少なくとも2週間必要でしょう。
sentence_meaning: At least two weeks will be needed for this job.

mnemonic: A ghost on the right of it and a cloud alongside, and whatever the thing is, it carries on after the rest has stopped: たましい.
notes: 気 き is spirit as energy and 神 かみ is a god. 魂 is the soul of one particular person.
sentence: 彼の魂は永遠に生き続けるでしょう。
sentence_meaning: His spirit will live on for eternity.

mnemonic: Water 氵 wears away at a thing until there is none of it left, and your thumb does the same to the switch on the way out: けす.
notes: 消える きえる is the light going out by itself. 消す is you turning it off.
sentence: 教室を出る時は電気を消してください。
sentence_meaning: When you leave the classroom, please turn off the lights.

mnemonic: The word for how a thing is running, tuned 調 well or tuned badly, and today the body it belongs to is running badly: ちょうし.
notes: 状態 じょうたい is the state a thing is in, flatly. 調子 is how well it is going, and it is the word for how you feel.
sentence: 体の調子が良くないです。
sentence_meaning: My condition is not good.

mnemonic: Two hooks turned into one another so that neither of them does a thing alone. Trusting the other one is the whole business: おたがい.
sentence: お互いを信頼することが大事です。
sentence_meaning: It is important to trust each other.

mnemonic: The thing and the person resemble 似 each other closely enough to fit 合 together, and the kimono looks as though it were made for her: にあう.
notes: 似る にる is looking like something. 似合う is looking right alongside it.
sentence: 彼女は着物がよく似合います。
sentence_meaning: Kimonos suit her well.

mnemonic: An animal 犭 about the size of a seedling 苗 when you got it, and it owns the house now. I am extremely fond of them: ねこ.
sentence: 私は猫が大好きです。
sentence_meaning: I love cats.

mnemonic: Four legs, a tail, and an ear that goes up the moment your hand touches the door handle. He wants the poster with one on it: いぬ.
sentence: 犬のポスターが欲しいです。
sentence_meaning: I want a poster of a dog.
